title: Dusting and wiping high-touch surfaces
audience: Cleaners on short-stay, hotel-style and serviced-apartment turnovers who dust and disinfect rooms.
learningOutcomes: Dust a room from the highest point to the lowest, in a fixed order.
List the high-touch surfaces in a guest room and explain why they need disinfecting, not only wiping.
Apply an approved product so that the label's contact time is respected.

instruction.heading: Why dusting carries weight
instruction.body: A small amount of dust shows clearly on a dark or polished surface, and a guest who notices it may assume the rest of the room was not properly cleaned. Dusting is therefore a visible part of the standard, not a formality. It is done in one direction, from the highest points to the lowest, so that anything knocked down by one pass is caught by the next. Dry dusting is done before any wet work, so that wet cloths are not left with dust to push about.

instruction.heading: Top-to-bottom dusting in practice
instruction.body: Start with the high points: light shades, the tops of wardrobes and cupboards, artwork and picture frames, and fittings on the walls. Then work down through the window sills and blinds, the tops of furniture, the bedside tables and the desk, and finally the low items such as the base of lamps. Lampshades and light fittings are dusted only with the power off and the item cool and stable. Anything you cannot reach safely is reported under “Reporting damage and maintenance faults” rather than reached by improvised means. Use the dry or lightly damp cloth that your method sets, and avoid any tool that moves dust into the air.

instruction.heading: High-touch surfaces need disinfecting
instruction.body: High-touch surfaces are the points a guest's hands use most often: the remote control, the telephone, door handles inside and outside, light switches, drawer and cupboard handles, the mini-fridge door and handle, and the bedside controls. These need wiping with an approved disinfectant, used exactly as its label directs. The label states the contact time the product needs to work, and the surface must stay wet for that time. Wiping a surface and drying it at once does not satisfy the step unless the label allows it. A surface that looks clean may still need disinfecting.

instruction.heading: Cloth and product discipline
instruction.body: Apply the product to the cloth rather than spraying it onto electrical items, switches and the telephone. Keep the cloth just damp, so the surface is wet only where the label requires it. Fold the cloth to a clean face as you go. Replace the cloth when it is no longer picking up residue or when it has been used on a dirty area. Keep the zone coding from your business method, so that a cloth used in the bathroom does not reach the room's surfaces.

procedure: Confirm the product for each surface and the contact time on its label. Check the SDS if a product is unfamiliar.
Dust from the highest point in the room to the lowest, using the dry or damp cloth your method sets.
Include lampshades, artwork, picture frames, window sills, blinds and the tops of furniture.
Switch off and let cool any lighting before touching a lampshade or fitting. Report anything you cannot reach safely.
Wipe and disinfect the high-touch surfaces with the approved product, and leave the label's contact time before drying where required.
Clean the inside and outside of drawers, the mini-fridge door and handle, and the base of lamps.
Change cloths between zones and whenever a cloth is no longer clean.
Check each surface by sight and by touch before moving on, for streaks, residue and missed dust.

workedExamples.situation: A bedroom in a serviced apartment. The remote control, lamp switch and door handle look clean. The bedside table has a ring mark from a glass.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Is it enough to wipe the ring mark and move on?
workedExamples.reasoning: No. The ring mark needs removing with the approved product and method, and the remote, the switch and the door handle each need the disinfecting step as well. Check the label's contact time before drying or moving on, and confirm the ring mark has gone when you look at it at an angle.

equipmentAndPpe: Microfibre or other dusting cloths, as the method specifies
Approved disinfectant and surface products, with labels and SDS available
Gloves suited to the products in use
Step platform only where the property and the method allow it

commonErrors.error: Dusting from the bottom up, so that dust falls onto areas already done.
commonErrors.prevention: Work from the top of the room down, in one direction.

commonErrors.error: Spraying product directly onto the remote, telephone or light switch.
commonErrors.prevention: Apply the product to the cloth and wipe with a cloth that is just damp.

commonErrors.error: Drying a disinfected surface before the label's contact time has passed.
commonErrors.prevention: Read the label, and leave the contact time before drying or moving on.

commonErrors.error: Missing the inside of drawers, the mini-fridge door and its handle.
commonErrors.prevention: Use the high-touch list in the checklist rather than memory alone.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Disinfectants and cleaning products are used as the label and SDS direct. Mixing products, or using a product in a way its label does not allow, can cause harm.

Cleaning the exterior of a fitting is within this lesson only when it is isolated and cool. Any electrical work beyond wiping is licensed work in each state and territory. This lesson does not grant any electrical licence.

qualityStandard: Dust is removed from every listed high point before lower surfaces are dusted.
Every listed high-touch surface is wiped with an approved product, and the label's contact time is observed.
No streaks, product residue or visible dust remain on the surfaces checked.
documentationEvidence: Checklist showing each high-touch point ticked
Record of any surface that could not be cleaned, with the reason
summary: Dust from the top of the room down, using dry work first.
High-touch surfaces need an approved product and its full contact time, not a quick wipe.
Zone-coded cloths and a check by sight and touch keep the room free of carried-over dirt.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why are high-touch surfaces given a separate step in the room?
options: Guests touch them often, so they must be disinfected as well as look clean
They are the largest surfaces in the room and they need the most cleaning time
They are the only surfaces a guest will see and they should look neat at all times

knowledgeChecks.question: A cleaner sprays product straight onto a light switch and wipes it at once. What is the main problem?
options: The switch will be dusted twice and the wall will need wiping later
Product may enter the switch, and the label's contact time may not be met
Spraying is faster than using a cloth and it saves time on the room

knowledgeChecks.question: In what order should dusting be done?
options: Lowest surfaces first, then the highest
Highest surfaces first, then the lower surfaces
Floors first, then the highest surfaces
